stories.headline: Stadium denied, Congress gets alternative venue for Rahul Gandhi’s ‘Chhatron Ki Goonj’ event in Indore
stories.deck: The Indore Mayor stated that an old Madhya Pradesh High Court order restricts its use to sports or state-level government events
stories.bodyText:
After being denied permission to use the Indore stadium, the Congress on Friday (September 11, 2026) paid over ₹10 lakh to lease an alternative venue in the city for party leader Rahul Gandhi’s upcoming ‘Chhatron Ki Goonj’ programme.
Accusing the ruling BJP of deliberately delaying permissions out of panic, Congress leaders confirmed that the party secured a three-day lease of 12,000 sq metres of land in front of the Regional Park from the Indore Development Authority for the student outreach event.
An Indore Development Authority (IDA) official said that the land in front of the Regional Park has been temporarily leased to the Congress from September 17 to September 19, and the fee was fixed at ₹10.08 lakh as per the prevailing rates.
A letter from the IDA to Indore City Congress Committee President Chintu Chouksey stated that permission to hold the event would be issued after the deposit of the funds, subject to the prescribed conditions.
The letter also stated that the organisers would be responsible for ensuring necessary security arrangements at the venue and obtaining no-objection certificates from the relevant departments.
Talking to PTI, City Congress Committee President Chouksey said, “We have deposited the agreed amount into the IDA’s bank account.” He alleged that the BJP government was nervous about Gandhi’s upcoming event in Indore, and in this panic, it has been harassing the Congress over the venue.
“We initially wanted to hold the event at the Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium on September 12, but after not receiving permission, we had to change the date to September 19. We were made to run around for 10 days for the land located in front of the Regional Park,” Chouksey said.
The Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium, where the Opposition party initially sought permission for the programme, falls under the municipal corporation.
Indore Mayor Pushyamitra Bhargava said that under an old order of the Madhya Pradesh High Court, the stadium can only be used for sports or state-level government events.
The BJP’s state co-media in-charge Alok Dubey said that the Congress is indulging in propaganda politics and the public knows the truth about this party.
Taking a jibe at the Congress, he said the name of Gandhi’s event should be changed from “Chhatron Ki Goonj” to “Jhooth Ki Goonj”. Congress, meanwhile, has named its event venue as “Bharat Jodo Maidan” and claims that approximately 1.5 lakh students have registered for the programme.
“Chhatraon Ki Goonj” is a student-dialogue campaign launched by Mr. Gandhi to corner the BJP on issues such as question paper leaks, expensive education, irregularities in government recruitment, and unemployment.
Under Mr. Gandhi’s leadership, four editions of the “Chhatron Ki Goonj” programme have been organised so far in Kota, Dehradun, Prayagraj, and Pune.
The previous one held in Pune on August 22 was for female students.

stories.headline: Congress unable to digest India's progress, spreading negativity over BRICS: BJP
stories.deck: BJP MP and national spokesperson Sambit Patra said that while the "I" in BRIC was "turning shaky" in 2011-12, India is now one of the strongest partners of BRICS
stories.bodyText:
The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Friday (September 11, 2026) slammed the Congress and other Opposition parties for creating a "negative atmosphere" around the BRICS summit, alleging that they are unable to "digest" India's progress as the country moves forward.
The ruling party said that while in 2011-12, under the Congress-led UPA government, India appeared to be losing its position within BRICS, today all BRICS' heads of state are in India, and the country is celebrating the bloc "as never before." India is hosting the 18th BRICS Summit on September 12-13 at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi. A day earlier, the Congress questioned the benefits of hosting the BRICS Summit.
In a video message, BJP MP and national spokesperson Sambit Patra said that while the "I" in BRIC was "turning shaky" in 2011-12, India is now one of the strongest partners of BRICS. "Today, India has found its position in the global arena as never before," he said.
"Remember, the 'I' in BRICS stands for India, and the 'I' in India stands for the 140 crore people of India. I am India. I am one of the strongest partners of BRICS, and I am proud of it. Today, I am proud to be a citizen of India and a very strong member of BRICS," he added. Mr. Patra cited two articles published in leading newspapers in 2011 and 2012 to back his claim.
"Today, the Congress party and some Opposition parties are trying to spread negativity and create a negative atmosphere around the BRICS Summit. I think they need to be shown a mirror," he said.
Citing a 2012 article based on comments by global financial services firm Goldman Sachs, Mr. Patra said its headline was "India least attractive BRICS member in valuation terms." "Goldman Sachs clearly says that in 2012, if there was one BRIC member that was the least attractive in terms of valuation, it was India," Mr. Patra said.
He said when Jim O'Neill, then chairman of Goldman Sachs, was asked whether Brazil was the strongest BRIC country and India the weakest, he said India was the least attractive in terms of valuation.
"China would be the most attractive; India would be relatively the least... That being said, because the markets are so worried about India, as I mentioned earlier, if we do indeed get some reforms, perhaps India will further rally ahead of the move than the other markets. I have China as number one, probably right now, Brazil as number two, Russia is number three, and India is number four," Mr. Patra quoted O'Neill as saying.
He further said the final line of the article stated that it would not be a surprise if Indonesia replaced India, as Indonesia had moved far ahead.
"What is the essence of this article? It essentially says that in 2012, there were no meaningful reforms in India, the country was falling behind, inflation was high, and the condition of the Indian market was such that, among the BRIC nations, India was at the bottom," he said.
Mr. Patra said the second article, published on September 21, 2011, highlighted high inflation and a weak currency in India. "The second article is dated September 21, 2011, and its headline is, 'With high inflation and weak currency, India not like other BRIC countries'," he said.
"Inflation in India is the worst among the so-called BRIC nations. Current account deficit is a concern, fiscal deficit is a worry, fresh investments are stalled despite creaky infrastructure. Probably for the first time in a decade since Jim O'Neill of Goldman Sachs coined the acronym, BRIC is weakening and the ‘I’ in it turning shaky," Mr. Patra said, quoting further from the second article.
"And yet, we have some politicians and some Opposition leaders who are not able to digest this. Today, some members of the Opposition and the Congress party are unable to digest India's progress because India is moving forward," Mr. Patra added.

stories.headline: Decathlon India wholesale business grows 20-fold as B2B eyes big opportunity
stories.deck: Decathlon India wholesale business grows 20-fold as B2B eyes big opportunity
stories.bodyText: Bengaluru: Decathlon Sports India’s wholesale business has grown 20-fold in the last five years and now accounts for around 10% of the sports retailer’s total revenue, as the French sporting goods giant steps up its focus on institutional, corporate and smaller-city markets..The company’s B2B operations now reach more than 20,000 pin codes, covering over 90% of India. Tier-II and III markets, including Jammu & Kashmir, Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh and the Northeast, contribute more than 40% of its B2B revenue..The expansion is helping Decathlon extend its reach beyond its own stores through over 20,000 partners across India, including small retailers and resellers operating where it lacks a physical store..Tata Motors owned Jaguar Land Rover plans redundancies: Report.“Wholesale stands as a core growth pillar at Decathlon Sports India, now contributing about 10% of our overall business,” said Raghwendra Singh, Wholesale Director, Decathlon Sports India..Singh said local resellers are important in markets where consumers may otherwise have limited access to quality sporting products. “Though Decathlon now has a significant store network, our stores don’t cover the entire country,” he said, adding, “The role B2B plays today is to bring quality and affordable products across different geographies of India.”.Some retailers are also creating sports communities around their stores by organising activities and events, Singh said..Decathlon has expanded its institutional business through the Government e-Marketplace (GeM), where it operates as an OEM. It has fulfilled over 1,000 GeM orders, supplying expedition tents, cycles, footballs and field equipment to more than 500 government organisations and PSUs..Corporate demand.Its institutional business spans defence and police personnel through CSD Army Canteens and Kendriya Police Kalyan Bhandar, while its corporate operations serve over 20,000 companies and entities with workplace sports and customised gifting solutions. The company also supplies over 500 educational institutions, non-profits and community foundations..The broader B2B push comes as Decathlon sees growing interest in sports beyond cricket and football, including pickleball, skating, golf, fishing and horse riding..Corporate demand is increasingly moving beyond conventional bulk orders towards sports and wellness products, including yoga mats, mobility kits and equipment for emerging sports..“Corporates are increasingly coming to us with a particular sport or fitness activity they want to encourage,” Singh said, pointing to pickleball and other paddle sports. Some companies are supporting employees through memberships or sporting equipment..Decathlon has also introduced its ‘Gift a Sport’ initiative, wherein companies and institutions can opt for sports and wellness products instead of conventional corporate gifts. “It is also about changing the gifting culture and making sport a priority in people’s lives,” Singh told DH..The company is also using online marketplaces and quick-commerce platforms to widen its reach, with products available across more than 300 cities, while expanding its local manufacturing base.

stories.headline: Now, Coforge's Non-Executive Independent Director D K Singh resigns
stories.deck: Now, Coforge independent director DK Singh resigns
stories.bodyText: Bengaluru: Just days after OP Bhatt quit as chairman, Non-Executive Independent Director and Chairperson of the NRC (Nomination and Remuneration Committee) DK Singh has resigned from mid-tier IT services firm Coforge with immediate effect..Accordingly, he also ceases to be member of the Committees of the Company. There is no other material reason for his resignation, Coforge said in a BSE filing on Friday. He is not a director on the board of any other listed entity, and does not hold membership of any board committee of a listed entity..As interim Chair till January 31, 2027, Vivek Sharma will lead a global search for adding additional independent directors to the board. He will also oversee the process of electing the new Chair, which will consider both existing and newly appointed directors. The board has reconstituted NRC and Stakeholders’ Relationship Committee (SRC), and has designated Beth Boucher, Non-Executive Independent Director as the Chairperson of the NRC..After OP Bhatt, Coforge NRC chair DK Singh resigns citing differences, tension between directors.Meanwhile, Coforge’s internal audit had found that OP Bhatt’s Chairman category had received the lowest rating in the board evaluation exercise. But the finding was not disclosed before the board or the NRC when the evaluation results were presented, the company said in a BSE filing..“It is relevant to note that the observations of the internal auditor relate to the manner in which the reports and the findings arising from the Board Evaluation exercise were circulated, presented and discussed before the NRC and the Board by the NRC Chair and the Chairman of the Board,” it said..The relevant reports were available to the NRC Chair and the Chairman of the Board alone, but were not made available to other members of the board, including the independent directors, at the instruction of the Chairman of the Board, it further said.

stories.headline: 25 years of 9/11: Qaida releases video of Osama's son reportedly killed in 2019
stories.bodyText:
On the 25th anniversary of the Sept 11 attacks, al-Qaida's official media wing, As-Sahab, has released a propaganda video featuring the first-ever footage of Hamza bin Laden, the son and designated heir of Osama bin Laden. The video's release has drawn scrutiny from intelligence analysts, primarily because Hamza was reported to have been killed in a US counterterrorism operation along the Afghan-Pakistan border around 2019.
The 50-minute-long video titled "A Quarter Century of the 11 September Raids" also features unseen images of slain AQ chief Ayman Al Zawahiri. The outfit has not acknowledged his death to date or issued its customary funeral eulogy. The video aims to propagate the ideological doctrine associated with the current outfit chief, Saif al-Adl, with the Bin Laden name aimed at recruitment.
Intriguingly, the video opens not with international operations, but with historical footage from the Sept 2014 al-Qaida in the Indian Subcontinent attack on the Karachi naval dockyard. Intelligence sources noted that prioritising this regional operation underscores the influence of Pakistani terrorists within both al-Qaida's central leadership and its propaganda apparatus.
Visually, the footage, they said, was meticulously staged to evoke a sense of ideological nostalgia. Hamza appears multiple times in the footage, seated against a stark, cracked mud wall, clad in a traditional white turban with an assault rifle propped beside him. "The deliberate choice of staging serves a clear dual purpose: establishing Hamza's authority as his father's successor while invoking the classic visual identity of early global jihadism," said a source.

briefs.headline: UN chief Guterres meets PM Modi; discusses West Asia, Ukraine conflicts
briefs.deck: The Secretary-General appreciated India’s close cooperation with the United Nations.
briefs.bodyText:
UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres on Friday (September 11, 2026) held wide-ranging discussions with Prime Minister Narendra Modi on current conflicts in West Asia and Ukraine, with the world body chief reaffirming the principle of freedom of navigation.
Mr. Guterres met Mr. Modi in New Delhi on the sidelines of the 18th BRICS summit that Delhi is hosting on September 12-13. The two leaders "had a wide-ranging discussion on the current conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine, and the impact both are having on the global economy, including regarding access to food and fertiliser," the office of the Spokesperson for the UN Secretary-General said in a statement.
The Secretary-General appreciated India’s close cooperation with the United Nations.
It said the secretary-general "reaffirmed the principle of freedom of navigation.” The two leaders also exchanged views on the growing danger of lethal autonomous weapons. They also discussed the priorities of India's presidency of the BRICS, including the need for multilateral institutions that clearly reflect the realities of the world in the 21st century, the statement said.
The UN chief has been invited to speak at the summit's Open Session on ‘Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability: Shaping the Future for Inclusive Global Growth’ on September 13. India, a founding member of BRICS, is Chair for 2026 and will be hosting the 18th BRICS Summit, which will bring together leaders of member states and partner countries as well as outreach invitees.
Mr. Guterres, whose second five-year tenure as head of the United Nations ends in December 2026, had travelled to India in February to attend the India–AI Impact Summit 2026 in New Delhi.

briefs.headline: BRICS Finance Ministers & central bank chiefs voice concern about 'unilateral imposition' of tariffs
briefs.deck: The first Finance Ministers and central bank governors meeting under India’s chairship of BRICS was held on August 12, and the second was held on September 9-10 in Mumbai, following which a joint statement was issued
briefs.bodyText:
The Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors (FMCBG) of the BRICS nations collectively voiced their concerns about the “unilateral imposition” of tariffs and non-tariff measures that distort trade, in a joint statement issued on Friday (September 11, 2026).
The FMCBG also called for “practical solutions” to enhance cross-border payments in local currencies. However, they also acknowledged the primacy of national priorities in such matters and that there can be no “one-size-fits-all approach”.
The first FMCBG meeting under India’s chairmanship of BRICS was held on August 12, 2026, in Jaipur, and the second was held on September 9-10 in Mumbai, following which the joint statement was issued.
Concerns about tariffs
“We continue to have serious concerns with the unilateral imposition of trade- and finance-related actions, including the raising of tariffs and non-tariff measures, which distort trade and are inconsistent with World Trade Organisation (WTO) rules,” the joint statement said. “These pressures weigh most heavily on Emerging Markets and Developing Economies (EMDEs).”
While the joint statement did not mention the U.S., it is the only country that is actively engaged in levying extraordinary tariffs on its trade partners.
Also read: BRICS summit 2026 LIVE updates
The BRICS Finance Ministers and central bank governors also reiterated their support for an “open, transparent, inclusive, non-discriminatory, and rules-based” multilateral trading system with the WTO at its core.
Local currency trade
The FMCBG acknowledged the efforts of the BRICS Payment Task Force (BPTF) in exploring “pragmatic solutions” for efficient cross-border payment mechanisms.
“In this regard, we acknowledge the work done to study the cross-border interoperability of payment and messaging channels, and the discussions on promoting trade settlements and investments using BRICS local currencies, while respecting national priorities and acknowledging that there is no one-size-fits-all approach,” the joint statement said.
The FMCBG encouraged the payments task force to continue discussions to facilitate “practical solutions for cross-border payments among BRICS countries, which are fast, low-cost, more accessible, efficient, transparent, and safe”.
New taskforce for growth
India used its chairship to establish a BRICS Task Force on Growth and Development as a dedicated platform to address shared growth and development challenges of relevance to BRICS and other emerging markets and developing economies.
The Task Force is structured into two workstreams covering the Resilience, Innovation and Cooperation pillars, and the Sustainability pillar.
“We recognise the Task Force on Growth and Development as a platform that provides BRICS countries a space to discuss growth models suited to their own national contexts and development priorities, and encourage the continuation of its work, in alignment with the workstreams of Ministries of Finance and Central Banks,” the joint statement said.
The joint statement also covered other areas of discussion between the BRICS countries, such as the reform of multilateral lending institutions such as the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund, tax and customs cooperation between BRICS jurisdictions, central bank capacity building, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence and quantum computing in finance, and the global economy.

briefs.headline: Nearly 9 in 10 water samples in Gujarat villages unfit for drinking: CAG
briefs.deck: Water in 9 out of every 10 Gujarat village unfit for drinking: CAG
briefs.bodyText: Ahmedabad: The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG), in a report tabled in the Gujarat Assembly on Friday, said that a beneficiary survey carried out in 48 villages, covering 960 beneficiaries, revealed that nearly 89% — nearly nine out of every 10 — of water sample tests in the villages were found unfit for drinking.."Audit observed that out of 88 water samples collected from test-checked villages, as per the acceptable limit, 10 samples (11.36%) were found fit for drinking purposes while 78 samples (88.64%) were found unfit," said the report, which looked into implementation of the Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) from 2019-2020 to 2023-2024..The analysis of the water quality in seven villages revealed that the parameters most frequently exceeding the prescribed limits included total hardness (in 65% of samples), turbidity (63%), total dissolved solids (TDS) and total alkalinity (56% each), and presence of magnesium (50%)..These tests were conducted in Amreli, Anand, Bharuch, Dahod, state capital Gandhinagar, and Patan..Over 2K GPs in Karnataka could face drinking water scarcity this summer.The CAG report also flagged inadequate representation of women and Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (SC/ST) members in "paani samitis" — Village Water and Sanitation Committees (VWSCs) — in rural areas under the JJM, whose guidelines prescribe that each "paani samiti" ensure adequate participation of women — at least six women members — and maintain their representation at not less than 50% of the total membership..The report, presented in the Assembly on the last day of the three-day Monsoon session, stated that in nine paani samitis, the representation of women members was below the prescribed ratio, and five had no women at all..Similarly, under the JJM, members belonging to the SC/ST communities should constitute at least 25% of the total membership. During the audit, the report stated, the mandated representation was not found in 12 paani samitis. In seven of these samitis, there was not a single representation of the community..Another flaw the audit observed, based on 48 test-checked villages, was that the paani samitis were constituted in the general meeting of Gram Panchayats, where only their elected members are present, instead of Gram Sabha meetings, where all members are present..The state government responded by saying that membership to paani samitis was "voluntary and based on nominations or consent at the village level". It also stated that while isolated deviations had been noticed in the audit, the state was "committed to ensuring that all future constitutions" of paani samitis strictly followed the JJM guidelines..Paani samitis — consisting of 10-12 members — are established for the implementation of the JJM at the village level..Members include women, members of SC/ST communities, health workers, ASHA workers, and teachers, among others.

briefs.headline: Hanle: Making of a great astronomy hub
briefs.deck: Making of a great astronomy hub
briefs.bodyText: Indian astronomers have long explored the skies from observatories across the country. Now, Ladakh is emerging as a major focus, with existing and planned facilities at Hanle, Merak near Pangong Tso and other sites. The Indian Astronomical Observatory (IAO) at Hanle, one of the field stations of the Indian Institute of Astrophysics (IIA), is central to this expansion..“The IAO at Hanle will become a major hub for astronomy in the eastern hemisphere, with multiple facilities set up by various organisations in the country. It will become a multi-wavelength astronomical observatory with the largest telescopes in the country,” notes Prof. Annapurni Subramaniam, Director, IIA..A telescope to film the universe.At Hanle, about 4,500 metres above sea level, the cold, dry Trans-Himalayan desert, low atmospheric water vapour, dark skies, minimal light pollution and relatively stable atmospheric conditions make the site particularly well-suited to optical and infrared astronomy, as well as sub-millimetre and millimetre observations. .Its location away from the monsoon also provides clearer observing nights. The site has grown beyond a single telescope, with facilities such as the 0.7-metre GROWTH-India telescope, which adds robotic optical observing capability, HAGAR, and the Major Atmospheric Cherenkov Experiment (MACE), while Baba Atomic Research Centre explores additional sites in Ladakh..A wider astronomy ecosystem.“A decade from now, Ladakh will truly become a world-class astronomy hub. Hanle already hosts telescopes from gamma-ray (Cherenkov) to near-IR,” says Prof. Subramaniam. More telescopes in the sub-mm (Tera Hz) region are expected in the next 5-10 years, further broadening its capabilities. .Hanle and Merak are now poised for a new phase of expansion, with the proposed 13.7-metre NLOT and an upgraded HCT at Hanle, while the NLST is planned at Merak..NLOT at Hanle would be India’s most ambitious ground-based astronomy facility. With nearly 15 times the light-collecting area of existing 4-metre-class telescopes, it will allow astronomers to study fainter and more distant objects in greater detail. It is expected to bridge the gap between India’s current 3–4-metre-class telescopes and next-generation. Extremely Large Telescopes (ELTs), enabling detailed studies and rapid follow-up observations. The NLST will cover optical and near-infrared wavelengths, strengthening solar astronomy in Ladakh. The Hanle Dark Sky Reserve, meanwhile, protects the region’s exceptionally dark skies while promoting astronomy education and astro-tourism..“With NLST and NLOT, Ladakh will host major facilities for both daytime and nighttime observations and rank among the world’s leading observatory sites,” adds Prof. Subramaniam. The proposed NLST at Merak, she said, is expected to be the world’s second-largest solar telescope and could be operational within five years, boosting solar and space-weather capability..Ajay Talwar, who took up amateur astronomy when Halley’s Comet last appeared in 1986, is Vice-President of the Amateur Astronomers Association Delhi. He has witnessed Ladakh’s transformation since 2007. Recalling Hanle then, he says, “It was a largely undiscovered dark-sky site, with only a few lights visible in the villages around Hanle. The night sky was the best anywhere in India.” While looking for a cloud-free location to observe the occultation of Venus during the monsoon, he and fellow amateur astronomers discovered the IAO at Hanle..Maheswar Gopinathan, Professor, Astronomy and Astrophysics Group, IIA, says: “Ladakh could evolve into a multi-wavelength, multi-messenger astronomy hub. Its landscape could also enable high-altitude and near-space scientific experiments, supporting India’s ‘quantum leap’ into space. A future Telescope Park of 1-metre-class telescopes could further boost research, education, outreach and amateur astronomy.”.He notes that developing uHCT and NLOT could create local jobs in construction, logistics, hospitality and maintenance while improving infrastructure. They could also support science education, skills and training among youth through outreach and internships..Prof. Gopinathan says that the site’s extreme altitude, cold, low oxygen, temperature variations and remoteness pose major operational challenges. Transporting precision-engineered components and planning construction around seasonal weather add to the complexity. With no conventional grid power, Hanle’s scientific facilities rely solely on solar power, with diesel backup for other logistical needs..Hanle’s transformation into a globally competitive astronomical centre, he says, would require reliable, high-capacity infrastructure rather than treating facilities as standalone projects. Robust power systems, communications and data connectivity, better roads and logistics, workshops and accommodation and medical support suited to the high-altitude environment. A local technical workforce would also reduce dependence on personnel travelling from the plains for routine maintenance..Efficient remote observing, quick response to sudden astronomical events and reliable automated operations will be crucial. With the right infrastructure, Hanle could evolve into a full-fledged observatory ecosystem, with telescopes, instrument development facilities, laboratories, data centres and training facilities, supported by national and international collaborations..Telescopes alone will not make Ladakh an international astronomy destination. Prof. Subramaniam says many international institutions have shown interest in collaborations that could bring in technologies and help develop cutting-edge instruments..The red flags.But the expansion also raises concerns about protecting the dark skies that make Ladakh attractive to astronomers. “When I visited Hanle in 2007, there were only a few homestays. Today, the area has more than 80 homestays and much greater tourist activity,” says Talwar..While government support, astronomy festivals, telescopes at homestays and sustained promotion have brought more visitors to the region, he believes the growth is also affecting Hanle’s dark skies..Bright headlights from vehicles always disrupt night-time observations, while increasing tourist activity has added to waste-management concerns in remote areas. “The very popularisation of astro-tourism is bringing about the spoiling of the pristine environment in Ladakh,” he adds..Talwar says strict rules for the Hanle Dark Sky Reserve should be enforced, including curbs on night-time driving and better waste management. Tourists should also be educated and contribute towards the cost of removing waste from Ladakh’s sensitive areas..The real test will be whether Hanle can expand its scientific ambitions without losing the dark skies and fragile environment that made it special in the first place..(The writer is an independent science writer)

briefs.headline: Putin says European troop deployment in Ukraine would be ‘war against Russia’
briefs.deck: Putin said European leaders "are frightening their populations with an imaginary threat coming from Russia"
briefs.bodyText:
President Vladimir Putin warned on Friday (September 11, 2026) that any deployment of European troops to Ukraine would amount to "a war against Russia" and said Moscow did not "pose a threat".
"At the moment, they say they are considering how to send troops onto Ukrainian territory. That means a war against Russia," Russian news agencies quoted him as saying, referring to European leaders.
"We are not threatening and have no intention of threatening European countries. Why would we? No one even realises that we have no reason to enter into conflict with Europe," he said.
He said European leaders "are frightening their populations with an imaginary threat coming from Russia".
"This threat does not exist and has never existed," he added.
Russia launched a large-scale offensive against Ukraine in February 2022 and has repeatedly said the deployment of Western troops on Ukrainian territory was a red line that must not be crossed.
Such a deployment has been discussed by European leaders for several years but has never materialised.
Russia justifies its assault on Ukraine citing what is says is a threat posed by NATO's expansion to its borders, the Western military alliance that Kyiv aspires to join.
Published - September 12, 2026 06:29 am IST

briefs.headline: North Korea launches ballistic missiles toward sea after military drill it sees as threat
briefs.deck: North Korea’s Defence Minister criticised the U.S.-South Korea-Japan military drills, warning that North Korea could take “strong and reflective countermeasures from the standpoint of power”
briefs.bodyText:
North Korea launched ballistic missiles toward the sea on Saturday (September 12, 2026), its neighbours said, a day after the U.S., South Korea and Japan ended their trilateral military drill that North Korea views as a security threat.
South Korea’s military said it detected the launches of several missiles from North Korea’s eastern coastal Wonsan area. It said South Korea has boosted its surveillance posture and was closely exchanging information on the launches with the U.S. and Japan.
The U.S. Pacific Command said the North’s launch event does not pose an immediate threat to U.S. territory or to its allies. It said the U.S. remains committed to the defence of the U.S. homeland and allies in the region.
South Korea’s military said the five-day Freedom Edge exercise is defensive in nature and meant to enhance a joint response capability against North Korean nuclear threats.
Hours after the drill began on Monday (September 7, 2026), North Korea’s Defence Minister, Kim Song Gi, criticised the exercise and warned North Korea was capable of taking “strong and reflective countermeasures from the standpoint of power.”
Published - September 12, 2026 06:27 am IST

briefs.headline: ‘Swararchana’ seeks to make classical music a lived experience
briefs.deck: ‘Swararchana’ seeks to make classical music a lived experience
briefs.bodyText: Bengaluru: An evening of Hindustani classical music unfolded at the Prestige Centre for Performing Arts to a packed audience. This is also special because this is indeed the inaugural edition of ‘Swararchana’, a new annual cultural initiative by Deccan Herald and Prajavani. This brand new initiative aspires to bring music lovers closer to the country’s musical traditions..The auditorium remained visibly engrossed as flautist Prakash Hegde and santoor artiste Suma Hegde opened the programme with ‘Raga Yaman’, setting a quiet, attentive mood before Indian classical musician, singer and actor Rahul Deshpande took the stage..Deshpande, one of the most prominent contemporary voices in Hindustani music, presented ragas Koushi and Paraj, followed it up with shorter devotional compositions before and concluding the concert with a Nirguni bhajan. His performance brought together technical precision and an expressive vocal style, drawing the audience into the nuances of the compositions..‘Lau Suna Suna’ went viral after Nepal floods. But you may have missed its real meaning.Speaking about the idea behind ‘Swararchana’, Sowbhagyalakshmi K T, Director at The Printers Mysore Pvt Ltd (TPML), said the initiative was conceived in response to the increasingly noisy and fast-paced nature of everyday life..“We live in a world of constant noise and endless notifications. What we wanted to bring alive this evening is the power of music, and particularly classical music, to create a sense of mindfulness, to transform and move you from within,” she said..Sowbhagyalakshmi said the future editions would explore collaborations between traditional and contemporary artistes, including folk, independent, popular and experimental music. “We want our audiences to experience storytelling, folk performances, and immersive experiences inspired by our shared cultural history,” she said..The aim, she added, was to examine how Karnataka’s cultural heritage continues to shape the present.

stories.headline: Kin can appear for elderly, sick and overseas voters in Karnataka SIR process
stories.deck: Karnataka election officials have taken a notable step by allowing adult family members to represent vulnerable voters, aiming to streamline the rigorous revision process. Additionally, a new campaign targeting fresh 18-year-olds is on the horizon. Yet, obstacles in implementation and ongoing information deficits remain, resulting in a backlog of applications still in limbo due to unclear…
stories.bodyText:
BENGALURU: Karnataka’s Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) office has directed election officials to let adult family members appear on behalf of senior citizens, persons with disabilities, sick persons and overseas electors during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
The decision follows requests from voters and political parties, after the Election Commission on Friday permitted the arrangement. The family member must appear before the Electoral Registration Officer (ERO) or assistant ERO with the necessary documents.
Joint CEO S Yogeshwara said the step is to make the SIR process easier for electors who find it difficult to appear in person.
Separately, ECI has also planned a second special campaign on Sept 19 and 20 for voters who have turned 18 but do not have an EPIC card.
The CEO office has asked the district election officer (DEO) Bengaluru, the Chief Commissioner of Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA), DEOs and deputy commissioners across the state, and additional DEOs of BBMP Central, North and South election districts to instruct EROs and AEROs.
The instructions have been circulated to officials concerned in all the 224 assembly constituencies. The CEO office has also released photos and videos of officers reaching out to vulnerable voters to help them enrol.
The move is expected to ease pressure on vulnerable voters, but elderly and unwell citizens continued to queue up at hearing centres through the week, exposing a gap between the order and its implementation on the ground.
At the GBA office on 9th Main, HSR Layout, an 86-year-old woman with a pacemaker turned up in person, accompanied by her neighbour. “It was total chaos. Seniors waited for more than an hour in a token-based system. I began objecting, when the AERO said they could have just walked in. There was a lot of information gap up until then,” said Uma Mani.
By Friday, the CEO office had allowed family members to represent seniors at hearings, but lack of documents emerged as another hurdle. “We have kept their applications pending for now and are awaiting clarity on ways to navigate this,” said assistant ERO Geeta, at a school in Wilson Garden.

stories.headline: Beyond the canvas: Finding the soul of Indian art
stories.deck: Art curator Alka Pande speaks about India’s many colours, the rise of Gen Z collectors and the changing face of art during her visit to Bengaluru
stories.bodyText:
“I think art should always come from the heart. Art is something that moves you. Can AI move you all the time? I have my doubts,” says museum curator Alka Pande as she reflects on Bengaluru’s distinct art scene, AI in art and Gen Z collectors. An art connoisseur since childhood, Alka grew up in a home filled with music, dance, literature and poetry. Of late, she has been travelling across the country in search of unusual voices and new visual languages for the shows she is curating. “With so much war and strife happening, what are people looking for?” she asks. A pause, then the answer: “Beauty and tranquillity.”
‘Bengaluru vs Delhi: Two cities, two grammars of art’
“As a curator, I’m also a storyteller of art,” she says. Having spent years in Delhi, Alka finds the contrast between the artistic languages of Delhi and Bengaluru fascinating. “People in Bengaluru are influenced by culture, literature, mythology and stories. Artists often talk about their lives in their art. And the life of artists working in North India is very different from the ones in the South,” she notes.
Delhi, layered with politics, power and chaos, evokes a heavier visual response. In Bengaluru, she sees artists experimenting with natural pigments and colours, while telling stories rooted in their own communities. “When I string them together into a 
ragamala
 or a garland of stories, it becomes like a book of short stories,” she explains.
‘I delve deep into India and its many colours’
“Art, for me, is a reflection of society,” she says, adding, “Artists are, in some ways, documenters of society, of the climate and the ecosystem.” Bengaluru, she adds, has created an art ecosystem of its own rather than simply depending on the gallery circuits of Delhi and Mumbai. “I see a lot of students at the Karnataka Chitrakala Parishath creating their own work who are genuinely interested in art. There’s also the Bangalore Literature Festival happening. There’s theatre here,” she says. “When I visited the Indian Music Experience, for instance, I was gobsmacked. It’s beautifully done,” she beams with delight.
Her travels, she says, have deepened her love for India’s cultural diversity. “As I’m growing older and understanding my country more and more, I’m realising the cultural difference in this country. I feel it is not one India, it is many Indias,” Alka says. Different languages, cuisines, traditions and ways of life may divide the country geographically, she believes, but spirituality and philosophy create deeper connections. “Even though we may speak different languages, eat different foods and look different, spirituality and philosophy unify us and keep us together. India is like Europe. We have so much diversity. But there is unity in diversity.”
It is this diversity that continues to draw her towards Indian visual culture.
Even though we may speak different languages, eat different foods and look different, spirituality and philosophy unify us and keep us together.
Alka Pande
The way people collect art is changing too, particularly among younger buyers. “Gen Z views art very differently from older generations,” Alka explains. While traditional collectors often focus on beauty and craftsmanship, younger buyers are more drawn to quirkier and experimental work. “They are far more cosmopolitan because they are exposed to a wider range of ideas through their phones and social media,” she adds.
“Many artists are promoting their work on Instagram. They don’t even need galleries — it’s like a startup,” Alka says. As for the buyers, she explains, “Gen Z is very well-informed and aware. They know that owning an art piece is a part of their own identity and taste. They may not buy very expensive pieces of art but they buy very quirky and different art for their homes.” Alka adds, “Hundreds of people buy art, and many buy with an eye on the market. Many of them collect only as investments. Some people buy for the sheer joy of it. So it depends on what you are buying. But for the true lovers of art, they have a judicious balance of both investment and creativity.”
Gen Z is very well-informed and aware. They may not buy very expensive pieces of art but they buy very quirky art for their homes.
Alka Pande
A recent trip to Mysuru offered Alka another glimpse into the relationship between art and culture. She had travelled to the city to visit the Chamundeshwari Temple. “I’m a great worshipper of the Devi,” she says, but also took the opportunity to meet local artists. “The artists in Mysuru are very innovative and deeply connected to their environment. I saw artists experimenting with everything from traditional stone to modern beadwork,” she says. Alka was equally struck by the Jagannatha Centre for Art & Culture. “The architecture, the café, and the way art had been woven into every corner of the space, including a magnificent Nataraja sculpture, were inspiring,” she says.
Can AI create rasa?
Artificial intelligence, Alka says, is the art world’s next great challenge, although she admits she is still learning about the technology. “As a curator, that’s not easy to reckon with. I’m not such a great fan yet because I don’t know enough about it. But many artists are using it. Ultimately, it’s all about the prompts that a human gives the machine. I can’t say how beautiful and immersive AI art would be or how much 
rasa
 it would have. It can be immersive but would it have the same aesthetic enjoyment and aesthetic expression? I don’t know,” she says.

stories.headline: Bengaluru’s sweet shops offer low-sugar, diabetic-friendly treats as festive season rolls in
stories.bodyText:
Festive dining often leaves the health-conscious and diabetics navigating a field of sweet temptations. To keep everyone at the table, the city’s sweet shops are putting a modern spin on classic mithai by swapping refined sugar for alternatives like jaggery, dates, and natural substitutes.
What are the sugar alternatives used?
The “sugar-free” range of sweets use either alternative sugar substitutes made from natural ingredients or jaggery and dates. Asha Sweet Center, a landmark in Malleshwaram 8th Cross for 75 years now, offers two types of “sugar-free” sweets.
“We have sweets that have no form of sugar at all. In that category, we have our dry fruit barfi, where the sweetness comes from dates, figs, cranberries, and seeds. Similarly, we have dry fruit laddus and dry fruit bars,” said Darshini Mayur Garg, the managing partner of the brand.
“Then we also have sweets that are made with jaggery or sugar alternatives. The latter is diabetic-friendly, as these alternatives have no sugar and are low in calories,” Ms. Garg said. In that category, they offer besan laddus, Mysore pak, son papdi, and kaju barfi. “Our diabetic-friendly range is our way of making traditional Indian sweets more accessible to them without moving too far away from the flavours and textures they know and love,” she added.
India Sweet House has rolled out its modak for Ganesh Chaturthi. Shwetha Rajashekar, co-founder at the Bengaluru-based brand, said they had one variety made only of jaggery. “The outer layer of this modak is made of a jaggery kaju katli, and the filling has coconut and jaggery, similar to a holige,” she said.
This year, for International Women’s Day, the brand launched a new sweet called Sanjeevani Barfi, which has no sugar in it. The sweet is made of dry fruits, dates, figs and almonds, along with pumpkin and cucumber seeds. “The sweetness is derived from the dates and the figs that we have used,” she said, adding that the sweet is available all year round.
Another popular chain, Kanti Sweets, also has a sugar-free range. Here, they use jaggery and dates as sweeteners. Their zero-sugar dry fruit laddus are prepared exclusively with dates as sweeteners. Along with this, they also sell kaju katli and peda, sweetened only with jaggery, with no added sugars.
Is there demand for these sweets?
Asha Sweet Center said they have definitely seen growing interest in this category, adding that customers today are more conscious about what they consume, but that doesn’t mean they want to give up the traditions associated with festivals.
Ms. Garg explained, “There is a mixed crowd that also feels that when you are having a sweet, you might as well have it in its best form. It is a personal choice. People who have health or dietary restrictions choose to buy these sweets.” She also believes that Indian sweets are inherently healthy with the use of premium ingredients such as dry fruits, whole grains, and ghee. “Once in a while, you can indulge,” she said.
Ms. Rajashekar agrees: “Mithai is always associated with indulgence. You may control how much you eat. If you indulge in it every day, then you are conscious about your intake. But during festivals, we generally see an uptake in overall mithai sales, not specifically these. Festivals are to celebrate!”
(With inputs from C. Madan Mohan)

stories.headline: SIR in Karnataka: Adult family members allowed to attend hearings for senior citizens, PwD, sick, overseas electors
stories.deck: So far, only the person against whom a notice was issued was required to attend the hearing
stories.bodyText:
The office of the Chief Electoral Officer (CEO), Karnataka, has directed election officials to allow adult family members of senior citizens, persons with disabilities (PwD), sick and overseas electors to appear before Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) or Assistant Electoral Registration Officers (AEROs), on their behalf, to submit documents and information for disposal of notices issued to them.
The direction was issued by Joint Chief Electoral Officer S. Yogeshwara on September 11.
This follows a backlash over the handling of cases of prominent persons from various fields, with hearings being conducted at the convenience of VIPs in their houses, while those needing assistance, such as senior citizens, sick and overseas voters, who cannot travel to the hearing venue or are not in the country, had to appear in person.
So far, hearings at several venues highlighted the difficulties faced by senior citizens and persons with disabilities. Many, in last five days, were seen waiting for hours at crowded hearing venues: first to reach the ERO, then to have their notices scanned and documents checked. Several said they were unclear about which documents were required and whether originals or copies had to be submitted. In many cases, electors had to make repeated trips to get additional documents and return to the venue in case those documents were found insufficient, or have their hearings rescheduled.
The EROs and AEROs have now been told to explain the procedure followed for issuing and disposing of notices during their weekly meetings with political parties. The instruction applies to the District Election Officer, Bengaluru and Chief Commissioner, Greater Bengaluru Authority, District Election Officers, and Deputy Commissioners across Karnataka, as well as election officials in the three BBMP election districts, and Bengaluru city corporations.
So far, only the person against whom a notice was issued was required to attend the hearing, where documents were to be submitted. Under this system, many electors had cited reasons, such as old age, medical condition, hearing timing clashing with work hours, or being outside the country, for inability to attend the hearing. Now, an adult family member of a senior citizen, sick elector, overseas elector, or person with a disability, can appear for the hearing on their behalf.
Other voters have to mandatorily appear for the hearing in person.
As on September 10,43,81,760 notices had been generated as per ECI data. As many as 24,97,075 notices are yet to be delivered, resulting in an overall delivery percentage of 56.99%. With regard to hearings, 7,03,710 delivered notices have been heard while 17,93,365 are yet to be heard.

briefs.headline: Karnataka govt fills potholes near MS Bldg with jet-patchers
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: Govt Friday launched a pothole-filling exercise in one of Bengaluru’s VIP areas by deploying a jet-patcher — specifically used to spray-fill surface-level potholes without affecting traffic — on Devaraj Urs Road, which hosts MS Building (home to hundreds of bureaucrats and Karnataka Lokayukta) and just minutes from the twin Soudhas.
Bengaluru development minister Krishna Byre Gowda picked this road to demonstrate the new machine and watched the exercise. The machine uses cold mix asphalt for repairs. Gowda said this machine would be useful for potholes that are not deep, but cautioned that no single method could address Bengaluru’s widespread pothole problem.
The minister said hot-mix asphalt had limitations as it requires a roller and cannot be deployed frequently since it requires the full load. This technology will be extended to the other four city corporations based on its performance, he added.
The stretch assumes significance as it connects Ambedkar Veedhi with Basaveshwara Circle and is used by thousands of govt officials and visitors to Vidhana Soudha, CAG office, Karnataka Information Commission, Karnataka Public Service Commission and Legislators’ Home.
But for commuters, the problem has been less about the method of repair and more about how quickly repeated patches on this road deteriorate.
“Roads in front of Vidhana Soudha are well maintained. Right behind it, we had to drive over potholes and patchwork every day. We have seen several repairs on this road, but the patches come off very soon. The situation is worse during rain,” said Rakesh S, a driver.
“Potholes on this road would grow and cracks widen. But the unannounced pothole-filling exercise on Friday was a surprise,” an official working at MS Building said.
Parking attendant Nagaraj said two-wheelers often fell after hitting potholes on the stretch. “All top officers drive through this road, but they did not have the concern to get it repaired and maintained well,” he said.
GBA plans to deploy 5 jet-patcher machines from Sept 2026 to Sept 2027 to repair 14,041sqm road surface at a cost of Rs 2.5 crore. Repairing every square metre with this method costs Rs 1,448.

briefs.headline: Bengaluru lake lights stay on till 9 p.m., driving birds away
briefs.bodyText:
While lakes such as Dorekere and Doddakalasandra are important night-time shelters for hundreds of birds, a change in the lighting schedule at these lakes has been disturbing roosting spaces, with Kere Mitras (residents who protect, maintain, and monitor the lake) pointing out that the extended artificial lighting, now kept on till 9 p.m., is disturbing birds that arrive at the lakes at dusk to roost. Bright lakeside spotlights blind and confuse them, causing birds to lose their way, they say.
Lights that were earlier switched off by 7 p.m. now stay on until 9 p.m., after the installation of the centrally-monitored lighting through CCMS smart meters at the lakes. Kere Mitras and NGOs working on lakes say applying the same timing to lakes ignores ecological function, particularly in the evening when large numbers of birds return to sleep.
The concern is particularly worrisome at Dorekere lake, where birds arrive in large numbers in the evening and settle on the island and surrounding trees for the night. A biodiversity study by ActionAid, in association with the Australian Consulate General, Bengaluru, recorded 63 resident species and 11 migratory species at the lake between July 2023 and May 2024.
The lighting, volunteers say, makes the lake less attractive as a roost because birds use the onset of darkness as a cue to settle down for the night. Keeping the area brightly lit for another two hours can keep birds active, particularly when the lights fall directly on the trees or the island where they roost. Birds may then eventually move to darker parts of the lake or look for another roost altogether.
Raghavendra B. Pachhapur of ActionAid said the lighting schedule earlier allowed the lake to become dark relatively soon after dusk. He argued that it was not about preventing residents from using the lakes in the evening, but about treating a lake ecosystem in the same way as a conventional public space.
Dorekere’s bird records show that the lake is not simply a place where birds just pass through. Species such as Glossy Ibis, Cattle Egret, and Black-headed Ibis have been observed using the island to roost during the non-breeding season, even though they have not been recorded breeding there. The Glossy Ibis numbers increase significantly around mid-October, with up to 620 birds recorded roosting on the island.
At Doddakalasandra too, ActionAid’s recent survey recorded 46 bird species in a single day during March this year. Volunteers like Soundararajan Rajagopalan, a Kere Mitra for Doddakalasandra lake, pointed out that migratory birds visit Bengaluru between October and March, and the lake attracts both water-dependent and tree-dependent species.
The impact of artificial lighting is not limited to birds choosing a different tree for the night. A roost is part of a larger habitat, and repeated disturbance can change how birds use a lake over time, he said. “If you continue to do that, it disturbs birds and they will not consider this as a home and it has to switch places,” Mr. Rajagopalan said, adding that with this small change, we are pushing birds again to go outskirts.
GBA officials, however, said that the lights were set on an auto-timer till 9 p.m. to avoid any kind of illegal activity and to make the public feel safe as the lakes are usually open till 7.30 p.m. to 8 p.m., depending on the location.

briefs.headline: CJP flags poor teacher deployment due to SIR duty, sanitation concerns after Karnataka school visits
briefs.deck: The delegation raised their findings in a meeting with Karnataka Education Minister Madhu Bangarappa
briefs.bodyText:
After surveying more than 50 government schools in Karnataka as part of its national ‘School Thik Karo’ campaign, the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) said that around 80% of them suffer from unsanitary conditions.
While the CJP Karnataka team has been visiting schools for about a month, CJP co-convenor Ashutosh Ranka and CJP national secretary Afreen Nawaz, along with the team, visited four government schools in Bengaluru in the last few days.
The team, after interacting with students, staff and teachers at government schools in J.P. Nagar, Marathahalli, Yeshwantpur and Government Urdu School, Varthur, flagged a shortage of teachers due to SIR duties, unhygienic toilets, and a lack of infrastructure as some of the main issues.
Teachers away
According to Mr. Ranka, eight of nine teachers in the Sarjapur school were assigned SIR duties, and three of four teachers at the Marathahalli school were on SIR duty.
“A teacher’s time is precious, and five months of a calendar year are being wasted. The Election Commission should come up with an alternative plan,” Mr. Ranka criticised.
Hygiene and infrastructure
At the school in Marathahalli, the team noted that toilet hygiene was a major concern. At the J.P. Nagar school, while infrastructure was generally good, washroom conditions needed attention, they said.
“The school administration has reported a lack of budget for cleaning staff. The cleaning staff comes only once a week,” Mr. Ranka said.
He noted that the infrastructure at the Varthur school was severely dilapidated. “Around 150 children are studying in two classrooms. In one of the rooms, the ceiling was found to be on the verge of falling. Repair work began after our intervention,” he said.
Ms. Nawaz said that during their outreach on social media, youth from the State also reported Karnataka Public Service Commission recruitment issues as a major problem. The team called out to the public to join hands with them and to report schools in their locality that need attention.
The delegation raised their findings in a meeting with Karnataka Education Minister Madhu Bangarappa.

briefs.headline: Amid opposition, Karnataka govt. to take up 120-km elevated corridor network in Bengaluru
briefs.deck: The agenda for the city highlights that the government is currently in the process of inviting tenders for 11 of the proposed corridors, covering 75.60 km, at an estimated cost of ₹13,262.70 crore
briefs.bodyText:
Amid continuing controversy over Bengaluru’s elevated corridors and other large infrastructure projects, Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on Thursday reviewed plans for 13 elevated corridors spanning 120 km.
The agenda for the city showed that the government is currently in the process of inviting tenders for 11 of the proposed corridors, covering 75.6 km, at an estimated cost of ₹13,262.7 crore, according to details presented at a review meeting.
It was also been decided that the Bangalore Development Authority (BDA) will take up land acquisition for the elevated corridors. A survey of properties likely to be affected by land acquisition for the 11 corridors had already been undertaken.
The elevated corridors had been proposed to reduce congestion on major roads and junctions, improve connectivity between Bengaluru’s core and outer areas, and cut travel time. Most of the projects had been planned in line with the Bengaluru Integrated Transport Plan-2020, Mr. Shivakumar pointed out in the meeting with Greater Bengaluru Authority officials.
The Chief Minister was reviewing works under all parastatals as the GBA marked one year earlier this month. Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda was also present during the meeting.
Economic Development Agency
The meeting also dealt with the proposed Economic Development Agency, which was supposed to be set up within one year of the GBA’s formation, with the Minister for Bengaluru Development as its chairperson. The agency can be tasked with attracting investments and generating employment in the GBA limits through suitable public-private partnership projects.
The agenda mentioned that the proposal for the agency was placed before the GBA Executive Committee at its second meeting on July 3. Members were asked to submit suggestions or instructions within three days. As no suggestions were received, the proposal was subsequently submitted to the GBA Authority for approval.
₹1,700 crore road works
The review also covered white-topping works covering 120.69 km across Bengaluru at a total cost of ₹1,700 crore. Of this, 55.54 km is being taken up under the State government’s ₹800-crore grant for 2023-24, while another 65.15 km is being developed using ₹900 crore from additional tax revenue of the municipal corporations. So far, 64.09 km of roads have been completed and opened to traffic, while work on the remaining stretches is under way.

briefs.headline: Citizens continue to question logic, ecological cost of Hebbal short tunnel in Bengaluru
briefs.deck: Hydrologist Shashank Palur of WELL Labs said the use of 3.5 acres of Hebbal Lake needed closer scrutiny as Bengaluru’s lakes form a cascading system, with water flowing from one lake to another
briefs.bodyText:
Pointing to the Hebbal short tunnel’s use of 3.5 acres of Hebbal Lake and the removal of at least 893 trees along 2.2 km, citizens and activists have questioned whether the ₹1,140-crore project is the right solution to ease Bengaluru’s traffic problems.
The concerns were raised at a discussion organised by the Hebbal Nature Society and hosted by independent bookstore Kadhaigal on Thursday, where questions were raised over the project’s safety, environmental impact and whether existing and proposed public transport could offer alternatives to the tunnel.
The proposed tunnel is intended to ease congestion at the Hebbal junction. However, Rajkumar Dugar, founder and convenor of Citizens for Citizens, pointed out that the tunnel would be 2.2 km long, compared to about 1.8 km for the surface road between the same points. “Tunnels are usually opted for to shorten distances, to save ecological areas above ground or to bypass extreme terrains, but none of these scenarios hold good in this case,” he said.
Mr. Dugar also raised concerns over four sharp curves in the tunnel, flooding risks, varying driving speeds and air pollution arising from ventilation issues, arguing that the project did not even have the approval of the Bengaluru Metropolitan Land Transport Authority (BMLTA).
Hydrologist Shashank Palur of WELL Labs said the use of 3.5 acres of Hebbal Lake needed closer scrutiny as Bengaluru’s lakes form a cascading system, with water flowing from one lake to another. The discussion also pointed to flooding around Manyata Tech Park during the monsoon and raised concerns over the impact on Nagawara Lake and groundwater.
The project’s impact on the University of Agricultural Sciences (UAS), Hebbal campus, was another major concern. Ecologist and biodiversity researcher Hareesha A.S. said the campus was among the remaining diverse green spaces in north Bengaluru that have woodlands, grasslands, agricultural fields and wetlands. Pointing out that at least 893 trees are expected to be removed for the project, Mr. Hareesha also questioned tree transplantation as a mitigation measure, saying its success rate was extremely poor.
Residents also spoke about poor public transport and last-mile connectivity in the area, with many participants pointing out that buses did not connect some inner roads of the neighbourhood to the main roads, highlighting gaps.

briefs.headline: Mini AC buses for all Namma Metro stations in Bengaluru for last-mile connectivity
briefs.deck: BMTC live tracking app to be shared with cab aggregators
briefs.bodyText:
Mini air-conditioned (AC) buses will be deployed to areas within a 5-km radius of all metro stations.
Transport Minister Byrathi Suresh made the announcement after holding a meeting with senior officials of the Transport Department, KSRTC and BMTC at Vidhana Soudha on Tuesday.
A release said that of the 4,500 electric buses being provided to BMTC under the Central government’s PM E-DRIVE scheme, the Minister instructed that 200 mini air-conditioned (AC) buses be used to provide connectivity within a 5-km radius of all metro stations.
The buses will connect residential areas in the farthest parts of the city to metro stations, making travel more convenient for Bengaluru residents, it added.
The Minister also said BMTC will provide more air-conditioned buses to IT and BT companies in Bengaluru to reduce the use of private vehicles by their employees. He said officials have been instructed to hold discussions with the companies in this regard.
Namma BMTC app for aggregators
He also announced that the ‘Namma BMTC Mobile App 2.0’ will be made available to commercial passenger vehicles operated through apps such as Ola, Uber and others. Through this, passengers travelling in Ola and Uber vehicles will be able to easily obtain information about BMTC buses that operate to the destinations where they get off, the release said.
The release also stated that he issued instructions officials to take necessary measures to prevent revenue leakage in government-owned transport corporations, including BMTC, and gave clear directions to curb unnecessary expenditure.

stories.headline: Report: MSMEs need digital infra
stories.bodyText:
MUMBAI: NPCI Bharat BillPay has proposed a centralised digital infrastructure to connect invoices, payments, reconciliation and financing, to fix the biggest constraints faced by MSMEs - the difficulty of turning sales into cash and cash flows into credit. The system could help address the MSME sector's Rs 60 lakh crore formal credit gap, while reducing the friction involved in collecting and matching payments.
The proposed infrastructure would digitise the order-to-cash cycle through standardised APIs and automate reconciliation across more than 20 crore monthly GST e-invoices. Buyer-confirmed invoices could become financeable records, allowing lenders to assess borrowers on the strength of their cash flows rather than relying only on collateral. A common information layer could also reduce the mismatches that contribute to delays in MSME receivables.
According to a report by NPCI Bharat BillPay and Bain & Company, formal credit of around Rs 34 lakh crore meets only part of an estimated Rs 92 lakh crore demand for MSME debt, leaving a gap of around Rs 60 lakh crore. The shortage is greatest among smaller enterprises, where formal channels meet only 30% to 40% of debt demand.

stories.headline: Consumer durables drive customer growth
stories.bodyText:
MUMBAI: India's retail credit market is showing a widening gap between the number of borrowers being added and the value of loans being accumulated, with consumer durable loans driving new borrower acquisition, while home and gold loans account for much of the portfolio growth.
According to credit bureau CRIF's 'How India Lends' report, gold loan outstandings jumped 62.2% to Rs 21.7 lakh crore, while home loan outstandings rose 10.5% year-on-year to Rs 45.5 lakh crore in Q1 FY27. Yet origination volumes (new disbursements) for gold loans fell 4.5% year-on-year to 3.7 crore, while home loans grew by a modest 6.4% to 8.3 lakh. Quarter-on-quarter, gold and home loan volumes dropped 25.6% and 17.3%, respectively.
Consumer durable loans, however, grew both in volume and value. The origination volume grew 27.4% year-on-year to 2.9 crore, while the origination value grew 36.6%, with portfolio outstanding reaching Rs 1.2 lakh crore as of June 2026 from Rs 89,300 crore a year earlier. Consumer loans also defied the seasonal trend, growing 21.4% from Rs 1,00,500 crore as of March 2026. Consumer durables accounted for 45.5% of all new-to-credit borrower volumes in India, more than twice the share of gold loans at 18.3% and personal loans at 18.2%.

stories.headline: Cochin Shipyard, Drydocks World join hands to expand ship repair facility
stories.deck: The agreement follows a memorandum of understanding (MoU) signed between the two companies during India Maritime Week 2025 to explore cooperation in ship repair and allied maritime services
stories.bodyText:
Cochin Shipyard Ltd. (CSL) and UAE-based Drydocks World, a DP World company, on Friday (September 11, 2026) signed a joint venture agreement to operate and expand the International Ship Repair Facility (ISRF) at Cochin, in a move aimed at strengthening India’s ship repair capabilities and positioning the country as a global maritime services hub.
Union Minister for Ports, Shipping and Waterways Sarbananda Sonowal and UAE Assistant Foreign Minister for Advanced Science and Technology Omran Sharaf Alhashimi witnessed the signing on the sidelines of the BRICS Summit here.
The 50:50 joint venture agreement was signed by Drydocks World CEO Rado Antolovic and CSL chairman and managing director Jose V.J.
The statement issued by the Ministry reads that under the partnership, the two companies will operate, consolidate and expand the ISRF, creating additional capacity to service a wider range of vessels and cater to the growing requirements of Indian, regional and international customers.
The agreement follows a memorandum of understanding (MoU) signed between the two companies during India Maritime Week 2025 to explore cooperation in ship repair and allied maritime services. The companies described the new venture as a first-of-its-kind public-private partnership in India’s ship repair sector.
“The partnership between Cochin Shipyard and Drydocks World marks an important milestone in strengthening India’s ship repair ecosystem and reflects the enduring maritime relationship between India and the UAE,” Mr. Sonowal said.
He said the collaboration would combine India’s growing shipbuilding and repair capabilities with the UAE’s global maritime expertise and create new capacity, skills and economic opportunities.
The partnership is expected to strengthen Cochin’s position as a maritime services hub and generate opportunities in ship repair, engineering, fabrication and allied services in Kerala.
Mr. Antolovic said the venture would combine CSL’s local expertise and skilled workforce with Drydocks World’s global capabilities and technology. He said the company saw opportunities to expand ship repair and fabrication capabilities beyond the Cochin facility.
Strategically located along major international shipping routes, the ISRF has a ship lift system and modern docking facilities capable of servicing a wide range of vessels.
Both companies will hold an equal 50% stake in the joint venture, with the initial capital to be funded through equity contributions from the two partners.

stories.headline: India’s forex reserves jump by a record $44.903 billion
stories.deck: In the previous reporting week, the overall reserves increased $11.475 billion to a new all-time high of $740.803 billion
stories.bodyText:
“India's forex reserves jumped by a record $44.903 billion to a new lifetime high of $785.706 billion during the week ended September 4, 2026,” the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) said on Friday (September 11, 2026).
In the previous reporting week, the overall reserves increased $11.475 billion to a new all-time high of $740.803 billion.
The kitty had been declining since the start of the conflict in West Asia earlier this year, as the Rupee came under pressure and the RBI had to intervene in the forex market through dollar sales.
However, the reserves started increasing since the RBI announced concessional forex swap initiatives in June this year amid a sharp depreciation in the local currency. The move has yielded more than $136 billion in new flows.
For the week ended September 4, foreign currency assets, a major component of the reserves, increased $47.498 billion to $648.168 billion, the Central bank's data showed.
Expressed in dollar terms, foreign currency assets include the effects of appreciation or depreciation of non-U.S. units, such as the euro, pound, and yen, held in the foreign exchange reserves.
“Value of gold reserves decreased $2.594 billion to $113.816 billion during the week,” the RBI said, adding that the special drawing rights (SDRs) were down by $4 million at $18.806 billion. India's reserve position with the International Monetary Fund was up $2 million to $4.916 billion at the end of the reporting week, according to the Central bank's data.
